resume: Length of the leave, notice periods for your employer, daily allowances paid by the CSSM and documents to send, plus the new additional birth leave.
aQuoiCaSert: Paternity and childcare leave (congé de paternité et d'accueil de l'enfant) allows the father, or the mother's spouse, PACS partner (civil partnership) or cohabiting partner, to stop working after the birth to look after the child. During this leave, the employment contract is suspended and, in Mayotte, it is the CSSM (Caisse de sécurité sociale de Mayotte, Mayotte's social security fund) that may pay daily allowances. The national Labor Code (code du travail) has applied in Mayotte since January 1, 2018.
quiEstConcerne: The mother's spouse, PACS partner or cohabiting partner, if not the father.
These rules concern the private sector: civil servants, self-employed people and other schemes have their own rules.
aSavoir: Separated parents: the father is entitled to it with no requirement of marriage, PACS or living with the mother.
Length: 25 calendar days for a birth (32 for multiple births), in addition to the 3-working-day birth leave. A 4-day period is mandatory right after the birth leave.
The remaining 21 days (28 for multiple births) can be taken all at once or in 2 periods of at least 5 days, within 6 months of the birth.

Tell your employer at least 1 month before the expected date of delivery, then at least 1 month before the start of each period. Doing so in writing is advised: registered letter, or hand delivery against a signed receipt.
Daily allowances: in Mayotte, they are paid by the CSSM, reachable at 02 69 61 91 91 (service-public.gouv.fr).

Additional birth leave: since July 1, 2026, each parent can take 1 to 2 months of paid leave after maternity or paternity leave, for a child born on or after January 1, 2026. A decree of May 30, 2026 set out the arrangements for employees in Mayotte.
